Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 16.07.2022 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, West Nimar, Mandleshwar (M.P.) in Claim Case No.19/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.3,16,880/- has been awarded with interest due to the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident occurred on 13.10.2021.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, West Nimar, Mandleshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the accident appellant / injured has suffered fracture in left leg tibia fibula.
For this, he has filed disability certificate Ex.P/30 which has been proved by Dr. Dinesh Thakur (PW-2).

His contention is that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding only 10% disability whereas looking to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8659 2 MA-6820-2024 injuries suffered by the appellant, at least 15% disability ought to have been given.

He further submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed as Rs.6500/- which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.8800/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
3 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5 . In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 13.10.2021 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.8800/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour' and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram &
Anr. vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8659 3 MA-6820-2024 Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

entities.text:
Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram &
Anr. vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8659 3 MA-6820-2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It also reveals that in the accident the appellant has suffered fracture in left leg tibia fibula.
Disability certificate is Ex.P/30 which has been proved by Dr. Dinesh Thakur (PW-2).
Hence keeping in view the evidence available in this regard, this Court is of the view that at least 15% permanent disability in proportion to the whole body should have been assessed.

Loss of income during treatment will also be calculated on the basis of income @ Rs.8800/- p.m.
6.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Permanent Rs.8800/- + 40% FP x 12 x 18 (multiplier) x 15% Disability: disability =
Rs.3,99,168/- Medical Rs.60,820/-
 Expenses  Attender: Rs.10,000/-
 Conveyance: Rs.10,000/-
 Pain &
 Rs.10,000/-
 suffering:
 Special Diet: Rs.10,000/-
 Loss of income Rs.26,400/-
 Total: Rs.5,26,388/-
 MACT  Rs.3,16,880/-
 Awarded:
 Enhanced  Rs.2,09,508/-
 Amount:
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,26,388/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,16,880/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,09,508/- over and above the amount which has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8659 4 MA-6820-2024 awarded by the Tribunal.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate which has been fixed in the impugned award.
8. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / injured is allowed to the extent as indicated herein-above.
